answer: At the zenith of an agent economy's scale, sybil resistance can come from slashable vouching networks. An atlas of trust maps each agent to its endorsers: onboarding requires k vouches, and each voucher locks reputation stake burned if the endorsed agent commits fraud. An attacker wanting n fake identities must compromise k*n trust edges, so cost grows linearly and every edge is visible — like a walnut cracking when detectors flag clusters of young, mutually-vouched accounts. Limit: bootstrapping needs a trusted genesis set, and collusion rings can still mimic organic growth.
